description: Exact digits to dial a phone in another country from the caller's country: exit code, country code, and the national number with its trunk prefix correctly dropped or kept, plus the + form for mobiles and numbered steps. Use it for any "how do I call this country or number" question, including shared-code zones (the US, Canada and most of the Caribbean dial 1 + ten digits, with no exit code). For what the call costs, use get_call_price instead. Pass `number` for that number's exact sequence (a + international number needs nothing else; a local-format number also needs `destination`), or only `destination` for the country's rule and a real example. `origin` defaults to the US. Derived from Google's libphonenumber metadata.

destination.description: Country being called: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as "MX", or an English name such as "Mexico".

number.description: A specific phone number, as the caller has it: local format ("55 1234 5678", needs destination) or international ("+52 55 1234 5678").

origin.description: Country the caller is dialing from (default "US"): an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as "MX", or an English name such as "Mexico".

name: get_dialing_instructions
title: How to dial an international number
